_format_notes.purpose: One scenario = one hand-crafted claim with a known-correct expected verdict, per testing-and-evaluation-plan.md's 'Golden set' spec: 25-50 scenarios spanning all 5 claim categories x 3 fraud-risk bands x 3 image-consistency levels. Run on every CI push; any mismatch fails the build.

optional_but_needed_for_specific_metrics.reference (semantic similarity, Q9): reference_reasoning.image_parsing / reference_reasoning.decision -- an agent's free-text reasoning is graded by embedding-similarity against these, not exact string match, since paraphrasing shouldn't fail a scenario
optional_but_needed_for_specific_metrics.expected_entities (NER correctness, Q9): the claim-relevant entities an agent's output should mention -- order_ref, product, claim_category, refund_amount_usd -- catches a right label with wrong-order/wrong-product reasoning
optional_but_needed_for_specific_metrics.expected_tool_calls (tool routing + sequ: per-agent expected tool call set AND order -- e.g. redact_photo before analyze_image, never after
optional_but_needed_for_specific_metrics.reference_policy (RAGAS, Q22): which real docs/refund_policy.md chunk_id search_refund_policy should retrieve, for context precision/recall/faithfulness scoring
optional_but_needed_for_specific_metrics.photo_fixture: path to a real test image under tests/fixtures/ -- required whenever claim_category needs a photo and expected.image_verdict is not 'no_photo'

_format_notes.adversarial_note: Q13/Q20: a separate adversarial set runs alongside the regular golden set -- several distinct variants per protected mechanism (e.g. multiple claims crafted to push toward 'approve' on a refund over $200, each must still be forced to 'escalate'). scenario_type='adversarial' scenarios add an expected_guardrail_catch field naming which guardrail must fire.
_format_notes.matrix_cell_note: one of the 5 claim_category x 3 fraud_risk_band x 3 image_consistency combinations this scenario exists to cover -- tracked so golden-set coverage of the real decision matrix (project-plan.md/docs/refund_policy.md) can be verified directly, not just eyeballed from the scenario count.

scenarios.description: Straightforward, low-risk damage claim with clear photo evidence -- decision matrix says consistent+low => auto-approve. Baseline happy-path scenario.

input.claim_description: The box arrived crushed on one corner and the item inside is cracked.

reference_reasoning.image_parsing: The photo shows the ordered product with a visible crack consistent with transit damage; the item matches the product ordered.
reference_reasoning.decision: Photo evidence is consistent with the damage claim, fraud risk is low, and the claim was filed within the 30-day return window, so it is auto-approved for a full refund to the original payment method per the Damaged in Transit policy clause.
